source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

lines.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.
lines.zh: 哈囉，這裡是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。我是 Neil。

lines.en: And I'm Georgie.
lines.zh: 我是 Georgie。

lines.en: Some kids hate eating broccoli.
lines.zh: 有些小孩討厭吃花椰菜。

lines.en: For others, it's mushrooms.
lines.zh: 有些則是討厭香菇。

lines.en: And worst of all, of course, are Brussels sprouts!
lines.zh: 當然，最糟的是球芽甘藍！

lines.en: Every parent of young children knows what food they will and won't eat.
lines.zh: 每個有小小孩的父母都知道，孩子什麼東西肯吃、什麼不肯吃。

lines.en: What food did you dislike as a child, Georgie?
lines.zh: Georgie，你小時候不喜歡吃什麼？

lines.en: Ooh, when I was little, I used to absolutely hate nuts and avocados.
lines.zh: 喔，我小時候非常討厭堅果和酪梨。

lines.en: But now, as an adult, I absolutely love both of those things.
lines.zh: 但現在長大了，這兩樣我都超愛。

lines.en: I'm not surprised – they're delicious!
lines.zh: 我不意外——它們很好吃！

lines.en: What about you, Neil?
lines.zh: 那你呢，Neil？

lines.en: Did you dislike any foods?
lines.zh: 你有不喜歡的食物嗎？

lines.en: Do you know what? I think I liked most things.
lines.zh: 你知道嗎？我想我大部分東西都喜歡。

lines.en: Family dinner time can be fun – a chance to reconnect, hear about everyone's day and share a meal.
lines.zh: 家庭晚餐時間可以很有趣——是重新聯繫感情、聽聽每個人今天過得如何、一起吃飯的機會。

lines.en: But when children refuse to eat the food that's been cooked, the result is often conflict rather than family fun.
lines.zh: 但當孩子拒絕吃煮好的食物時，結果常常是衝突，而不是家庭歡樂。

lines.en: BBC Radio 4 programme The Food Chain asked child nutritionist and mother of two Charlotte Stirling-Reed whether her kids eat everything she gives them.
lines.zh: BBC 第四電台節目《The Food Chain》問兒童營養師、也是兩個孩子的媽媽 Charlotte Stirling-Reed，她的孩子會不會把她給的東西都吃完。

lines.en: They definitely don't.
lines.zh: 絕對不會。

lines.en: We go through multiple periods of ups and downs where their appetite is much lower, and then all of a sudden it comes right back.
lines.zh: 我們會經歷好幾段起起伏伏的時期，有時他們食慾很差，然後突然之間又完全恢復。

lines.en: It depends on the weather, what they've been doing that day.
lines.zh: 這取決於天氣、他們那天做了什麼。

lines.en: It can depend on their mood.
lines.zh: 也可能取決於他們的心情。

lines.en: At dinner time, Charlotte's children go through ups and downs, a phrase meaning that a mixture of good and bad things happen to them.
lines.zh: 在晚餐時間，Charlotte 的孩子會經歷 ups and downs（起起伏伏），這個片語的意思是好事和壞事交替發生。

lines.en: Sometimes they eat everything happily.
lines.zh: 有時候他們開開心心地全部吃完。

lines.en: Other times they don't.
lines.zh: 有時候則不會。

lines.en: It depends on many things, including their day, the weather and their mood.
lines.zh: 這取決於很多事，包括他們這一天過得如何、天氣和心情。

lines.en: A person's mood is the way they are feeling at a particular time.
lines.zh: 一個人的 mood 是指他在某個時候的感受。

lines.en: So, how can parents make dinnertime something everyone enjoys?
lines.zh: 那麼，父母要怎麼讓晚餐時間成為大家都享受的時光？

lines.en: In this episode, we'll be hearing from three experts on young children's eating habits and learning some useful new words and phrases too.
lines.zh: 在這一集，我們會聽三位幼兒飲食習慣專家的分享，也會學到一些實用的新單字和片語。

lines.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary from this episode, along with a quiz and worksheet, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 別忘了，這一集的所有詞彙以及測驗和學習單，都在我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com。

lines.en: But first of course, Georgie, I have a question for you.
lines.zh: 不過首先，Georgie，當然我有個問題要問你。

lines.en: Charlotte Stirling-Reed is a child nutritionist and she has some tips for stress-free family meals.
lines.zh: Charlotte Stirling-Reed 是兒童營養師，她有一些讓家庭用餐不緊繃的訣竅。

lines.en: Which of these do you think she recommends?
lines.zh: 你覺得她推薦的是哪一個？

lines.en: Is it: a) make sure your child eats five pieces of fruit and veg a day, b) don't pressure your child to eat everything on the plate, or c) introduce your child to lots of new flavours quickly?
lines.zh: 是：a) 確保孩子每天吃五份蔬果、b) 不要逼孩子把盤子裡的東西全部吃完，還是 c) 很快讓孩子嘗試很多新口味？

lines.en: That's quite hard. They all seem like quite good tips.
lines.zh: 好難喔。每一個聽起來都是不錯的建議。

lines.en: I'm going to go with c) introduce your child to lots of new flavours quickly.
lines.zh: 我要選 c) 很快讓孩子嘗試很多新口味。

lines.en: OK. We'll find out the answer later in the programme.
lines.zh: 好。我們會在節目稍後揭曉答案。

lines.en: Dr Anne Fishel is another expert in child nutrition.
lines.zh: Anne Fishel 博士是另一位兒童營養專家。

lines.en: She co-founded the Family Dinner Project, an organisation promoting children's healthy eating in the US.
lines.zh: 她共同創辦了「家庭晚餐計畫」，這是一個在美國推廣兒童健康飲食的組織。

lines.en: Here, Anne explains one reason why mealtimes can become stressful, to Ruth Alexander for BBC World Service programme The Food Chain.
lines.zh: 在這裡，Anne 向 BBC 世界廣播節目《The Food Chain》的 Ruth Alexander 解釋用餐時間會變得緊繃的一個原因。

lines.en: Many parents say dinnertime can become a battleground, so why is it that what you're eating can trigger so much tension?
lines.zh: 很多父母說晚餐時間可能變成戰場，為什麼吃什麼這件事會引發這麼多緊張？

lines.en: I think for small children it's one of the few areas that they have control over.
lines.zh: 我想對小孩來說，這是他們少數能掌控的領域之一。

lines.en: I mean, parents can cook what they want and serve it when they want, but it's up to kids to decide whether they're going to eat it.
lines.zh: 我是說，父母可以想煮什麼就煮什麼、想什麼時候上菜就什麼時候上，但吃不吃是孩子自己決定的。

lines.en: And for young kids, that's a big deal.
lines.zh: 對小小孩來說，這是件大事。

lines.en: They have some control.
lines.zh: 他們有一些掌控權。

lines.en: Dinnertime often becomes a battleground – a place where argument or conflict happens.
lines.zh: 晚餐時間常常變成 battleground——發生爭吵或衝突的地方。

lines.en: Anne thinks that's because it's one of the few areas where children have control.
lines.zh: Anne 認為那是因為這是孩子少數能掌控的領域之一。

lines.en: For kids, controlling what they're willing to eat is a big deal – something of special importance to them.
lines.zh: 對孩子來說，掌控自己願意吃什麼是 a big deal——對他們特別重要的事。

lines.en: If experts like Charlotte and Anne struggle at mealtimes, imagine how hard it could be if your child has a food allergy – a condition where the body makes you sick after eating certain foods.
lines.zh: 如果連 Charlotte 和 Anne 這樣的專家在用餐時間都會頭痛，想像一下如果你的孩子有食物過敏會有多難——這是一種吃了某些食物後身體會不舒服的狀況。

lines.en: That was the experience of Sharon Wee, a food writer from Singapore, who speaks here with BBC World Service programme The Food Chain.
lines.zh: 這是新加坡的美食作家 Sharon Wee 的經驗，她在這裡接受 BBC 世界廣播節目《The Food Chain》的訪問。

lines.en: My daughter was born with allergies and it was quite a struggle at first.
lines.zh: 我女兒天生就有過敏，一開始真的很辛苦。

lines.en: And to be honest with you, we found the winning formula, which was rice and beans, and she grew up eating rice and beans probably for the first five years of her life.
lines.zh: 老實跟你說，我們找到了致勝的組合，就是米飯配豆子，她大概人生的前五年都是吃米飯配豆子長大的。

lines.en: Sharon's daughter's allergies restricted what she could eat, making cooking for the whole family a struggle.
lines.zh: Sharon 女兒的過敏限制了她能吃的東西，讓幫全家煮飯變得很辛苦。

lines.en: Luckily, Sharon discovered the winning formula – something her daughter could safely eat – rice and beans.
lines.zh: 幸好，Sharon 發現了 winning formula——她女兒可以安全吃的東西——米飯配豆子。

lines.en: A winning formula is a method or strategy that produces successful results.
lines.zh: winning formula 是能帶來成功結果的方法或策略。

lines.en: So, Georgie, how can parents help their children develop good eating habits?
lines.zh: 那麼，Georgie，父母要怎麼幫孩子養成良好的飲食習慣？

lines.en: Well, there are some things that our experts all agree upon.
lines.zh: 嗯，有幾件事是我們的專家都同意的。

lines.en: For one, give children a choice – for example, by offering small, healthy snacks and dips before the meal.
lines.zh: 第一，給孩子選擇——例如在正餐前提供少量健康的點心和沾醬。

lines.en: And most importantly of all, create a stress-free atmosphere by not pressurising kids to finish everything on their plate.
lines.zh: 最重要的是，不要逼孩子把盤子裡的東西全部吃完，營造一個沒有壓力的氣氛。

lines.en: Right. Well, that also helps with your quiz question, Neil, so why not go ahead and reveal the correct answer?
lines.zh: 好。這也剛好跟你的問題有關，Neil，那就請你揭曉正確答案吧？

lines.en: I asked you what child food nutritionist Charlotte Stirling-Reed recommends for stress-free family meals.
lines.zh: 我問你兒童營養師 Charlotte Stirling-Reed 推薦哪一種讓家庭用餐不緊繃的做法。

lines.en: Yes. I said c) introduce your child to lots of new flavours quickly.
lines.zh: 對。我說 c) 很快讓孩子嘗試很多新口味。

lines.en: I'm afraid you were wrong, Georgie.
lines.zh: 很遺憾，你答錯了，Georgie。

lines.en: The answer is actually b) don't pressure your child to eat everything on the plate.
lines.zh: 答案其實是 b) 不要逼孩子把盤子裡的東西全部吃完。

lines.en: Ah.
lines.zh: 啊。

lines.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with ups and downs – a phrase describing the mixture of good and bad things that happen to someone.
lines.zh: 好。我們來複習學到的詞彙，首先是 ups and downs——形容一個人遇到好事與壞事交替發生的片語。

lines.en: Your mood is how you feel at a particular time.
lines.zh: 你的 mood 是你在某個時候的感受。

lines.en: A battleground is a place or situation where argument or conflict happens.
lines.zh: battleground 是發生爭吵或衝突的地方或情況。

lines.en: If something is a big deal, it's of special importance to you.
lines.zh: 如果某件事是 a big deal，就是它對你特別重要。

lines.en: A food allergy is a medical condition where certain foods make your body sick.
lines.zh: food allergy 是某些食物會讓你身體不舒服的醫療狀況。

lines.en: And finally, a winning formula is a method or strategy that produces successful results.
lines.zh: 最後，winning formula 是能帶來成功結果的方法或策略。

lines.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to learn more vocabulary on the topic of food, you can head to our topic page on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 我們的六分鐘又到了，但如果你想學更多和食物有關的詞彙，可以到我們網站 bbclearningenglish.com 的主題頁。

lines.en: See you again soon.
lines.zh: 很快再見。

lines.en: But for now, it's goodbye.
lines.zh: 但現在要說再見了。

lines.en: Goodbye!
lines.zh: 再見！
